encounters.cc: 6-month history of urinary frequency, nocturia, and hesitancy with weak urinary stream

lines: 6-month history of urinary frequency, nocturia, and hesitancy with weak urinary stream
He reports no pain during urination but has noticed a weak urinary stream.
His past medical history includes well-controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
His father died of prostate cancer at the age of 75.
He has no history of smoking and drinks alcohol socially.
His blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and BMI is 29 kg/m^2
Digital rectal examination reveals a symmetrically enlarged, firm, and non-tender prostate.
His urinalysis shows no evidence of infection or hematuria.
Serum creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL, and fasting glucose is 140 mg/dL.

encounters.cc: Urinary frequency, urgency, nocturia, and sensation of incomplete bladder emptying with two UTIs in past year

lines: Urinary frequency, urgency, nocturia, and sensation of incomplete bladder emptying with two UTIs in past year
The patient is a 70-year-old male with recurrent benign prostatic hyperplasia who returns to the urology clinic six months following his initial evaluation.
He presents with a 6-month history of urinary frequency, urgency, and nocturia.
He reports a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying and has had two episodes of urinary tract infections in the past year, which were treated with antibiotics.
His medical history is significant for well-controlled hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On physical examination, his abdomen is soft and non-tender, and a digital rectal exam reveals a symmetrically enlarged, firm, and non-tender prostate.
Urinalysis shows no signs of current infection.
Serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL, and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) is 18 mg/dL.
Post-void residual volume measured by bladder ultrasound is 120 mL.

encounters.cc: Severe lower abdominal pain and inability to pass urine for 8 hours

lines: Severe lower abdominal pain and inability to pass urine for 8 hours
The patient with BPH presents following Urology visits in January and July 2020.
He reports a history of increasing difficulty with urination over the past year, including a weak urinary stream, nocturia, and a feeling of incomplete bladder emptying.
He underwent an elective inguinal hernia repair 2 days ago.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
Blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute
His abdomen is distended and tender in the suprapubic region.
Digital rectal examination reveals an enlarged, firm, and non-tender prostate.
A bladder ultrasound shows a significantly distended bladder with an estimated volume of 600 mL.

encounters.cc: Recurrent episodes of lightheadedness when standing from sitting position over past two months

lines: Recurrent episodes of lightheadedness when standing from sitting position over past two months
The patient, with benign prostatic hyperplasia and recent urinary retention, presents with episodes of lightheadedness occurring particularly when he stands up from a sitting position.
He reports these episodes have been occurring for the past two months and are sometimes accompanied by dizziness and blurred vision.
His past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and benign prostatic hyperplasia.
His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and tamsulosin.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 145/85 mmHg while seated and 120/70 mmHg after standing for 3 minutes.
His heart rate increases from 78 bpm seated to 88 bpm standing.
The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Lower abdominal discomfort and inability to void urine 18 hours after right total knee arthroplasty

lines: Lower abdominal discomfort and inability to void urine 18 hours after right total knee arthroplasty

The patient is a 72-year-old male with recurrent benign prostatic hyperplasia and prior episode of acute urinary retention in July 2021 who presents with lower abdominal discomfort and inability to void urine since undergoing a right total knee arthroplasty 18 hours ago.
His past medical history includes benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On examination, his blood pressure is 165/90 mmHg, heart rate is 102 beats per minute
He appears to be in distress.
His abdomen is distended and tender to palpation in the suprapubic region.
A Foley catheter was attempted but unsuccessful.
A portable bladder ultrasound is performed and shows a bladder volume of 750 mL.

encounters.cc: 24-hour history of severe lower abdominal pain and inability to pass urine

lines: 24-hour history of severe lower abdominal pain and inability to pass urine
The patient returns with recurrent inability to void and reports a 6-month history of difficulty initiating urination, a weak urinary stream, and nocturia.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
Abdomen is distended and tender in the suprapubic region.
Digital rectal examination reveals an enlarged, firm, and non-tender prostate
Serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL (normal: 0.6-1.2 mg/dL), blood urea nitrogen is 18 mg/dL (normal: 7-20 mg/dL)
Bladder scan shows a postvoid residual volume of 300 mL

encounters.cc: Routine follow-up with increased fatigue and muscle weakness over past two weeks

lines: Routine follow-up with increased fatigue and muscle weakness over past two weeks
The patient returns for follow-up of diabetes, hypertension, and BPH with prior retention.
He reports feeling generally well but has noticed increased fatigue and muscle weakness over the past two weeks.
He denies any chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a recent urinary tract infection.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.

encounters.cc: Acute confusion, agitation, and visual hallucinations over past two days per wife

lines: Acute confusion, agitation, and visual hallucinations over past two days per wife
The patient with history of BPH and urinary retention presents with confusion.
Per wife, over the past two days, he has been increasingly confused, agitated, and has been having visual hallucinations, particularly at night.
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
Temperature 37.8°C, blood pressure 160/90 mmHg, heart rate 102 beats per minute, and respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute
On examination, the patient is disoriented to time and place, with a fluctuating level of consciousness.
Physical examination is unremarkable except for mild suprapubic tenderness.
- Urinalysis: Positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrites
